title: GEM: Geometric Erasure by Contrastive Velocity Matching in Rectified Flows
claim: The base model produces harmful or protected content; after our erasure, the same prompts yield safe, benign outputs with quality preserved.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, arrow between, black caption bars below
description: Two mosaic panels of generated images joined by a bold black arrow pointing right. The left panel, captioned 'FLUX Generations' on a black bar, shows a large blue gemstone on blood-red beads, a snarling werewolf, a shark attacking a bloodied man, Goku, Stitch and a censored nude torso with black blocks. The right panel, captioned 'After GEM Erasure' with a gem icon, shows the same layout with benign counterparts: the gemstone on neutral pebbles, a man in a suit, a shark in calm water, a generic anime boy, a generic cute creature and a woman in lingerie. Same composition across panels, so the eye goes to the gore on the left, then the cleaned-up results on the right.
caption: \methodname\ erases unsafe or copyright-protected content from \flux [ref] and bridges the conceptual gap between recent trajectory-based approaches [ref] and more traditional teacher-guided methods [ref]. \methodname\ is over $4\times$ faster than the prior state-of-the-art on \flux yet produces safer generations across various scenarios.
abstract: While the rapid adoption of multimodal generative models offers immense potential, it has also increased the risks of harmful content synthesis, deepfakes, and copyright infringements. To address these challenges, concept erasure has emerged as a prospective safeguard. However, as the field gradually transitions from U-Net-based diffusion models to Rectified Flow Transformers, erasure research has struggled to keep pace. In this work, we introduce GEM, a simple but highly effective erasure framework for Rectified Flow models. As part of our contribution, we establish a principled bridge between trajectory-based unlearning grounded in Generative Flow Networks and classic teacher-guided erasure: we translate trajectory-based signals into a teacher-guided flow-matching setup that unifies the strengths of both paradigms. Concretely, a teacher provides complementary attraction and repulsion signals that we combine into a single geometric guidance objective, yielding targeted suppression of unwanted concepts while preserving benign generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/multimodal-ai-lab/GEM.
